mainTopic: The songs of the לויים in the בית המקדש (weekdays, שבת מוסף and מנחה), and the ten journeys of the שכינה and the exiles of the סנהדרין
overview: The amud opens by rejecting a proof from the previous amud about which song the לויים sang when they were unsure whether it was ראש השנה. Then a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא lists the שיר של יום for each day of the week. Each song is tied to what ה׳ created on that day, and the שבת song is tied to a future 'day that is all שבת.' רבי נחמיה disagrees and explains the שבת song as referring to the first שבת, when ה׳ rested. The גמרא connects their argument to a disagreement between רב קטינא and אביי over how long the world will be destroyed. Next it gives the songs of שבת מוסף (האזינו in six sections, הזיו לך) and שבת מנחה (שירת הים and שירת הבאר), and proves that one section was sung each שבת. Finally, רבי יוחנן teaches that the שכינה left the מקדש in ten stages, each proven from a פסוק, and that it waited six months in the wilderness for תשובה. The matching ten exiles of the סנהדרין begin here and continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier case was different: that song fit the day anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof that in a doubtful case the לויים sang the weekday song, because in that case the song was the correct song of the day no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because that song was the song of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down a proof brought just before. The case that was brought does not show what was done in every unsure situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof relied on a time they sang "הרנינו" when they were unsure whether it was ראש השנה. But "הרנינו" was the right song either way, whether it was a regular Thursday or ראש השנה. So this case proves nothing about other unsure cases, where they may not have sung any song at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; this marks that the case brought as proof does not really match.
Song; here, the perek the לויים sang in the בית המקדש.
Of its day; the song set for that particular day.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the weekday song was never sung on ראש השנה. It only says this one case cannot prove what happened in every unsure situation.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case just brought as proof, where the לויים sang "הרנינו" on a day they were unsure about.

phrases.english: because it is the song of its day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought at the end of the previous amud (30b).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove the opposite position.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the case brought as proof, the song was right for both possible days, so it cannot show a general practice for unsure cases.

steps.title: Sunday's song: the earth belongs to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי יהודה in the name of רבי עקיבא starts listing the daily songs. On Sunday they sang "לה׳ הארץ ומלואה", because on the first day ה׳ owned the world alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי עקיבא: On the first day, what did they say? "The earth is ה׳'s and all that fills it," because He acquired the world, gave it over, and ruled alone in His world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic connected to what came before. It quotes a ברייתא explaining which song the לויים sang on each day of the week, starting with Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each daily song matches what happened on that day of creation. On day one ה׳ made the world and was its only ruler, since no other beings existed yet. So the song speaks of the whole earth belonging to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא; introduces a teaching of the תנאים from outside the משנה.
In the name of; passing on a teaching from someone else.
He acquired and transferred; ה׳ took ownership of the world and gave it over for people.
Ruler; here, the only ruler in the world.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the שיר של יום that we still say every day at the end of שחרית.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
On the first day, what would they say?
"The earth is ה׳'s, and all that fills it,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:1

phrases.english: because He acquired and gave over
and was ruler in His world.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ראש השנה song question to a full list of the weekday songs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Sunday the לויים sang תהלים 24, because on the first day ה׳ owned and ruled the world alone.

steps.title: Monday's song: ה׳ is great
steps.stepSummary: On Monday they sang "גדול ה׳ ומהולל מאד", because on the second day ה׳ divided His creations and ruled over them as King.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second day, what did they say? "Great is ה׳ and very much praised," because He divided His works and ruled over them as King.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list with Monday's song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the second day ה׳ separated the upper waters from the lower waters. Dividing and arranging creation is shown as ה׳ acting as King over it, and this song praises Him as the great King.

keyTerms.meaning: He divided His works; separating the waters above from the waters below.

phrases.english: On the second day, what would they say?
"Great is ה׳ and very much praised,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 48:2

phrases.english: because He divided His works
and ruled over them as King.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Monday the לויים sang תהלים 48, because on the second day ה׳ divided His works and ruled over them.

steps.title: Tuesday's song: ה׳ stands among His people
steps.stepSummary: On Tuesday they sang "אלהים נצב בעדת אל", because on the third day ה׳ revealed dry land in His wisdom and prepared the world for His people.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the third day they would say: "God stands in the congregation of God," because He revealed the land with His wisdom and prepared the world for His congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with Tuesday's song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the third day the waters gathered and dry land appeared, so people would have a place to live. The song speaks of ה׳ standing among His "עדה", His congregation, and that land is where that congregation would later live.

keyTerms.meaning: He revealed the land; dry land appearing from under the water.
The world, the place where people live.

phrases.english: On the third day they would say:
"God stands in the congregation of God,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 82:1

phrases.english: because He revealed the land with His wisdom,
and prepared the world for His congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Tuesday the לויים sang תהלים 82, because on the third day ה׳ revealed the land and prepared the world for His people.

steps.title: Wednesday's song: ה׳, God of vengeance
steps.stepSummary: On Wednesday they sang "אל נקמות ה׳", because on the fourth day ה׳ created the sun and moon, and in the future He will punish those who worship them.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourth day they would say: "ה׳ is a God of vengeance," because He created the sun and moon, and in the future He will punish those who worship them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with Wednesday's song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This day's link is different from the earlier ones. The song is not about praising what was made. It looks ahead to people who would wrongly worship the sun and moon, and it promises that ה׳ will punish them.

keyTerms.meaning: To collect payment, meaning to punish.

phrases.english: On the fourth day they would say:
"ה׳ is a God of vengeance,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:1

phrases.english: because He created the sun and the moon,
and in the future He will punish those who worship them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Wednesday the לויים sang תהלים 94, because on the fourth day ה׳ created the sun and moon and will one day punish those who worship them.

steps.title: Thursday's Song: Birds and Fish Praise ה׳
steps.stepSummary: On Thursday the לויים sang 'הרנינו לאלהים עוזנו', because on the fifth day ה׳ created birds and fish to praise His name.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fifth day they would say: 'Sing aloud to God our strength,' because He created birds and fish to praise His name.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through the week and gives Thursday's song and its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier days: each song matches what ה׳ created on that day. On day five ה׳ created birds and fish, and their existence is itself a praise to ה׳, so the song is a song of joyful praise.

phrases.english: On the fifth day they would say:
"Sing aloud to God our strength"
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:2

phrases.english: because He created birds and fish
to praise His name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of daily songs, from Wednesday to Thursday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thursday's song is 'הרנינו לאלהים עוזנו', because on day five ה׳ created birds and fish, who praise His name.

steps.title: Friday's Song: ה׳ Finished His Work and Reigns
steps.stepSummary: On Friday the לויים sang 'ה׳ מלך גאות לבש', because on the sixth day ה׳ finished creating and ruled over everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the sixth day they would say: 'ה׳ reigns, He is clothed with majesty,' because He finished His work and ruled over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives Friday's song and its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once creation was complete on day six, ה׳'s kingship over the whole world was complete too. So the song for that day is about ה׳ reigning in full majesty.

phrases.english: On the sixth day they would say:
"ה׳ reigns, He is clothed with majesty"
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:1

phrases.english: because He finished His work
and ruled over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from Thursday to Friday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Friday's song is 'ה׳ מלך גאות לבש', because on day six ה׳ finished creation and ruled over it.

steps.title: שבת Song: A Day That Is All שבת
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the לויים sang 'מזמור שיר ליום השבת', and according to רבי עקיבא this refers to the future, a day that is entirely שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the seventh day they would say: 'A psalm, a song for the day of שבת,' for the day that is entirely שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list with the שבת song. Here the reason is not about creation; it points to the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All six weekday songs were explained by something ה׳ did during creation, in the past. The שבת song is explained by a future time that will be 'all שבת.' This change in pattern is exactly what רבי נחמיה will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: A day that is entirely שבת, meaning the future world

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'a day that is all שבת' as just meaning the weekly שבת. רבי עקיבא means a future time, and that is why the next steps talk about the world being destroyed.

phrases.english: On the seventh day they would say:
"A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos"
phrases.notes: תהלים 92:1

phrases.english: for the day that is entirely Shabbos.
phrases.notes: He is talking about a future time when everything will be rest, not about the weekly שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's list, but switches from a past-creation reason to a future reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת song refers to the future time that will be entirely שבת.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה Asks Why the שבת Song Is Explained Differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי עקיבא: why explain the six weekday songs by creation in the past, but the שבת song by the future?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: What did the חכמים see that made them divide between these chapters?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה objects to the way the ברייתא explained the songs. He is setting up his own explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weakness he points to is inconsistency: six songs look back to creation, and one suddenly looks forward to the future. He sees no reason to split them this way and will offer one consistent explanation for all seven.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא here
What did they see, meaning: what reason did they have?
Chapters, here the chapters of תהלים sung each day

phrases.english: רבי נחמיה said:
What did the Sages see
to divide between these chapters?
phrases.notes: The weekday songs were explained by the past, at creation, but the שבת song by the future. That is the split he is asking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רָאוּ חֲכָמִים לְחַלֵּק בֵּין הַפְּרָקִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inconsistency between step 8 and steps 2 through 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's future-based explanation of the שבת song
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every weekday song is explained by creation in the past, there is no reason to suddenly explain the שבת song by the future.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's Version: Days One Through Three
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה begins his own list, where every song refers to creation. Days one through three are explained as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: On the first day, because He acquired the world, gave it over, and ruled in His world. On the second, because He divided His works and ruled over them. On the third, because He revealed land with His wisdom and prepared the world for His people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה starts giving his own explanation. For the first three days, he agrees with the reasons already given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' signals his alternative approach. For days one to three nothing changes, because these reasons were already about creation. The real difference will only show up at שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired, and gave over to others

phrases.english: Rather:
On the first: because He acquired the world and gave it over
phrases.notes: He gave the world over to mankind.

phrases.english: and ruled in His world.
On the second: because He divided His works
and ruled over them.
On the third: because He revealed land with His wisdom
and prepared the world for His people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בָּרִאשׁוֹן — שֶׁקָּנָה וְהִקְנָה וְשַׁלִּיט בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבי נחמיה's alternative list after his objection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Days one through three are explained by ה׳'s acts of creation, just as before.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's Version: Days Four Through שבת, Because ה׳ Rested
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה finishes his list. Days four to six stay the same, but the שבת song is about ה׳ resting after creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourth, because He created the sun and moon and will one day punish those who worship them. On the fifth, because He created birds and fish to praise His name. On the sixth, because He finished His work and ruled over them. On the seventh, because He rested.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה completes his list. The only real change from רבי עקיבא is the reason for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, the שבת song refers to the first שבת, when ה׳ rested from creating. Now all seven songs match one pattern: each one is about what happened on that day of creation.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: the שבת song is about the future, a day that is all שבת. רבי נחמיה: the שבת song is about the past, when ה׳ rested after creation, so all seven songs follow the same pattern.

phrases.english: On the fourth: because He created the sun and moon
and will in the future punish those who worship them.
On the fifth: because He created birds and fish
to praise His name.
On the sixth: because He finished His work
and ruled over them.
On the seventh: because He rested.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי נחמיה's list and gives his new reason for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת song refers to ה׳ resting on the seventh day of creation.

steps.title: The Argument Depends on רב קטינא: One Thousand Years of Destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two תנאים argue about רב קטינא's statement that the world will exist for six thousand years and then be destroyed for one thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue about רב קטינא's statement, for רב קטינא said: The world will exist for six thousand years, and for one thousand it will be destroyed, as it says: 'And ה׳ alone will be exalted on that day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is behind the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי נחמיה by linking it to רב קטינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב קטינא, after six thousand years there will be one thousand years of destruction, like one שבת after six days. That fits רבי עקיבא, who said the שבת song is about a future 'day that is all שבת.'

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who taught about the world's six thousand years

phrases.english: And they argue about the statement of רב קטינא,
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי עקיבא and רבי נחמיה.

phrases.english: for רב קטינא said:
For six thousand years the world will exist
and for one thousand it will be destroyed,
as it says: "And ה׳ alone will be exalted on that day."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 2:11. The single 'day' is read as one thousand years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the root of the disagreement between רבי עקיבא (step 8) and רבי נחמיה (step 11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world will exist for six thousand years and be destroyed for one thousand, which fits a future 'day that is all שבת.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two explanations of the שבת song depend on a bigger question: how the end of days will look.

steps.title: אביי: Two Thousand Years of Destruction
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רב קטינא and says the world will be destroyed for two thousand years, based on 'יחיינו מיומים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It will be destroyed for two thousand years, as it says: 'After two days He will revive us.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the opposite view, which fits רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the destruction lasts two thousand years, it does not match one שבת day. So there is no future 'day that is all שבת' to sing about, and the שבת song must be about the first שבת of creation, as רבי נחמיה said.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב קטינא here
After two days He will revive us

steps.whatToRemember: רב קטינא (one thousand years of destruction) fits רבי עקיבא's future שבת. אביי (two thousand years) fits רבי נחמיה, who explains the שבת song by the first שבת of creation.

phrases.english: אביי said: For two thousand it will be destroyed,
as it says: "After two days He will revive us."
phrases.notes: הושע 6:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view opposite to רב קטינא, which matches רבי נחמיה's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world will be destroyed for two thousand years, so the destruction does not match a single שבת.

steps.title: What was sung at the שבת מוסף?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which song the לויים sang when the שבת מוסף offering was brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the מוסף offerings of שבת, what would they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: which song did the לויים sing for the extra שבת offering? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא talked about the daily song for each day of the week. Now it asks about the extra מוסף offering brought on שבת, which had its own song.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra offering brought on שבת and holidays

phrases.english: At the Mussaf offerings of Shabbos,
what would they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the weekday and daily שבת songs to the special שבת מוסף song.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which song the לויים sang at the שבת מוסף.

steps.title: רב: They sang האזינו in six parts
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן בר רבא in the name of רב says they sang שירת האזינו, split into six sections marked by the memory-word הזיו לך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן בר רבא said in the name of רב: "הזיו לך."
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the לויים sang שירת האזינו, split into six parts. The six letters of הזיו לך help you remember where each part begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter is the first letter of one section of האזינו: ה for האזינו, ז for זכור, י for ירכיבהו, ו for וירא, ל for לולי, כ for כי ידין. The answer is given as a short memory-word instead of a full list.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory-word: six letters, each starting one section of שירת האזינו
The song of משה in דברים 32

steps.confusionAlert: הזיו לך is not a phrase to translate as 'the glory is Yours.' It is just six letters that help you remember the six sections of האזינו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Anan bar Rava said that Rav said:
"HaZIV LaCh."
phrases.notes: Each letter starts a section of האזינו in דברים 32: האזינו, זכור, ירכיבהו, וירא, לולי, כי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שירת האזינו, sung in six sections marked by הזיו לך.

steps.title: The synagogue divides האזינו the same way
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא in the name of רב says the way האזינו was split in the בית המקדש is the same way it is split for the Torah reading in shul.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: In the way they are divided here, so they are divided in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a practical point: when פרשת האזינו is read in shul, it is split into the same six parts used in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This links the בית המקדש practice to a practice we still keep. The six עליות that split האזינו follow the same breaks as הזיו לך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for how פרשת האזינו is divided into עליות in shul today.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Chanan bar Rava said that Rav said:
In the way they are divided here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the six sections the לויים sang in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: so they are divided in the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second statement of רב that applies the six-part division to the synagogue reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six sections of האזינו read in shul follow the same breaks as in the בית המקדש.

steps.title: What was sung at שבת מנחה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which song the לויים sang at the afternoon תמיד offering on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the afternoon offering of שבת, what would they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks another question: what did the לויים sing at the afternoon offering on שבת? This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning song of שבת was already discussed (מזמור שיר ליום השבת), and the מוסף song was just given. Now the גמרא fills in the last song of the day.

phrases.english: At the afternoon offering of Shabbos,
what would they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 14, now about מנחה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which song the לויים sang at the שבת afternoon offering.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The Song of the Sea and the Song of the Well
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says they sang אז ישיר and מי כמוך (the two halves of שירת הים), and אז ישיר of שירת הבאר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: "Then sang" and "Who is like You" and "Then sang."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that at שבת מנחה the לויים sang three sections: the first half of שירת הים, the second half of שירת הים, and שירת הבאר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two songs that both begin אז ישיר. The first one is שירת הים, split at מי כמוך into two parts. The second אז ישיר is a different song, שירת הבאר in במדבר. So there are three sections total.

keyTerms.meaning: "Then sang": opening words of שירת הים, and also of שירת הבאר
"Who is like You": the middle of שירת הים, where its second section starts
The Song of the Well, במדבר 21

steps.confusionAlert: The two "אז ישיר"s are NOT the same song. The first is שירת הים in שמות; the last is שירת הבאר in במדבר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Then sang" and "Who is like You,"
phrases.notes: שמות 15:1 and שמות 15:11, the two halves of שירת הים.

phrases.english: and "Then sang."
phrases.notes: במדבר 21:17, the Song of the Well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three sections: two halves of שירת הים and שירת הבאר.

steps.title: All the sections in one שבת, or one each week?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask: were all these sections sung on one שבת, or was one section sung each שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Do they say all of these on one שבת, or perhaps each and every שבת they say one?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the sections, the גמרא asks how they were used. Did the לויים sing all of them every שבת, or just one section each week, going in order?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists were given as a set of sections: six for מוסף and three for מנחה. The open question is whether the whole set was sung at once or rotated one section per שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: They asked:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי כּוּלְּהוּ בְּחַד שַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Do they say all of these on one Shabbos,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֹּל שַׁבְּתָא וְשַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי חַד?
phrases.english: or perhaps each and every Shabbos they say one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the sections from steps 15 and 18 were scheduled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether all sections were sung every שבת or one section per שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: The second set cycles twice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי: by the time the first set finishes once, the second set has gone around twice. So they must have sung one section each שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי יוסי said: By the time the first finishes once, the second repeats twice. Learn from this that each and every שבת they say one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. רבי יוסי says the first set (מוסף) finishes one round while the second set (מנחה) goes around twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוסף set has six sections and the מנחה set has three. If one section is sung each שבת, then in six weeks מוסף finishes once and מנחה finishes twice. That only works if they sang one section per שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא brings a source to answer a question
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
Rabbi Yosei said:
By the time the first says one round,
phrases.notes: "The first" is the six-part מוסף set; "the second" is the three-part מנחה set.

phrases.english: the second repeats twice.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כׇּל שַׁבְּתָא וְשַׁבְּתָא אָמְרִי חַד,
phrases.english: Learn from this: each and every Shabbos they say one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to settle the question of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That one section was sung each שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי: the first set finishes once while the second set finishes twice, which fits only a one-section-per-week rotation.

steps.title: Conclusion: One section each שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: each שבת they sang only one section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof and closes the question. Each שבת, the לויים sang one section of each set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing challenges רבי יוסי's ברייתא, so the question is settled. The sections rotated week by week: האזינו over six weeks for מוסף, and the three מנחה songs over three weeks.
steps.whatToRemember: שבת מוסף: האזינו in six sections (הזיו לך). שבת מנחה: שירת הים in two sections plus שירת הבאר. Each שבת they sang just one section of each set, in rotation.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 20 as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each שבת only one section of each set was sung, rotating in order.

steps.title: The שכינה left in ten stages, and the סנהדרין was exiled in ten matching stages
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אידי quotes רבי יוחנן: the שכינה traveled ten journeys, known from פסוקים, and the סנהדרין was exiled in ten matching stages, known from tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אידי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the שכינה traveled ten journeys, as we learn from verses. Matching these, the סנהדרין was exiled ten times, as we know from tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new topic with a teaching from רבי יוחנן about the שכינה leaving the בית המקדש in ten steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parallel lists here. The שכינה's ten journeys are proven from פסוקים, while the סנהדרין's ten exiles are known from a received tradition. The point is that the two departures match each other, stage for stage.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Idi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The Divine Presence traveled ten journeys, as learned from verses,
and corresponding to them the Sanhedrin was exiled, as known from tradition.
phrases.notes: Here מִגְּמָרָא means a tradition handed down from teacher to student, not something learned from a פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not connected to the discussion of the לויים's songs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה left in ten stages (from פסוקים), and the סנהדרין was exiled in ten matching stages (from tradition).

steps.title: Listing the ten journeys of the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the ten stages: from the כפורת to a כרוב, to the other כרוב, to the threshold, courtyard, altar, roof, wall, city, mountain, wilderness, and finally up to its place in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ten journeys of the שכינה, learned from verses: from the כפורת to a כרוב, from one כרוב to the other, from the כרוב to the threshold, from the threshold to the courtyard, from the courtyard to the מזבח, from the מזבח to the roof, from the roof to the wall, from the wall to the city, from the city to a mountain, from the mountain to the wilderness. From the wilderness it went up and settled in its place, as the פסוק says: 'I will go and return to My place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's first line so it can explain it, and lists each of the ten stages of the שכינה's departure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves step by step outward: from the holiest spot (the כפורת) through the בית המקדש, out of the city, into the wilderness, and finally away from the world. The last stage is backed by a פסוק in הושע, 'I will go and return to My place.' The proofs for the other stages come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two golden figures on the ארון
Threshold, the doorway of the היכל
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The Divine Presence traveled ten journeys, as learned from verses:
From the Ark cover to the cherub, and from cherub to cherub,
and from the cherub to the threshold, and from the threshold to the courtyard,
and from the courtyard to the altar, and from the altar to the roof,
and from the roof to the wall, and from the wall to the city,
and from the city to a mountain, and from the mountain to the wilderness,
and from the wilderness it ascended and rested in its place,
as it is stated: "I will go and return to My place."
phrases.notes: הושע 5:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבי יוחנן's statement by listing the ten stages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stages are כפורת, כרוב, כרוב, threshold, courtyard, altar, roof, wall, city, mountain, wilderness, and then up to its place.

steps.title: Verses for the first stages: Ark cover, cherub, threshold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the first three moves with three פסוקים: God speaks from above the כפורת, He rides on one כרוב, and His glory goes up from the כרוב to the threshold.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the כפורת to a כרוב, from one כרוב to the other, and from the כרוב to the threshold, as it is written: 'I will meet with you there and speak with you from above the כפורת.' And it is written: 'He rode upon a כרוב and flew.' And it is written: 'The glory of the God of Israel went up from the כרוב it was on, to the threshold of the House.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the list and brings a פסוק to prove each stage, starting with the first three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק puts the שכינה on the כפורת. The second shows it resting on one כרוב. The third clearly describes it leaving the כרוב for the threshold. Together they trace the first steps of the שכינה moving away from the holiest place.

phrases.english: From the Ark cover to the cherub, from cherub to cherub,
and from the cherub to the threshold, as it is written:
"And there I will meet with you,
and I will speak with you from above the Ark cover,"
phrases.notes: שמות 25:22

phrases.english: and it is written: "And He rode upon a cherub, and flew,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 22:11. Notice it says one כרוב, so the שכינה can rest on just one of them.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And the glory of the God of Israel had ascended
from upon the cherub on which it was
to the threshold of the House."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 9:3

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכַּפּוֹרֶת לִכְרוּב, מִכְּרוּב לִכְרוּב, וּמִכְּרוּב לְמִפְתָּן — דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving the stages listed in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The first three stages: כפורת to כרוב, כרוב to כרוב, כרוב to threshold.

steps.title: Verses for the threshold to the courtyard, and the courtyard to the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the next two stages: the courtyard was filled with God's glory, and God was seen standing on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the threshold to the courtyard, as it is written: 'The House was filled with the cloud, and the courtyard was full of the brightness of God's glory.' From the courtyard to the מזבח, as it is written: 'I saw God standing on the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going down the list, bringing a פסוק for the fourth and fifth stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל shows the glory now out in the courtyard. The פסוק in עמוס places God on the מזבח, which stands in the courtyard. Each פסוק shows the שכינה one more step outward.

phrases.english: And from the threshold to the courtyard, as it is written:
"And the House was filled with the cloud,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶחָצֵר מָלְאָה אֶת נֹגַהּ כְּבוֹד ה׳״.
phrases.english: and the courtyard was full of the brightness of the Lord's glory."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 10:4

phrases.english: From the courtyard to the altar, as it is written:
"I saw the Lord standing on the altar."
phrases.notes: עמוס 9:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues proving the stages in order.
steps.raayaObject: Stages four and five: threshold to courtyard, courtyard to מזבח.

steps.title: Verses for the altar to the roof, the roof to the wall, and the wall to the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves three more stages: dwelling on a corner of a roof, God standing on a wall, and God's voice calling to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the מזבח to the roof, as it is written: 'It is better to dwell on a corner of a roof.' From the roof to the wall, as it is written: 'And behold, God was standing on a wall made by a plumb line.' From the wall to the city, as it is written: 'God's voice calls out to the city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings פסוקים for stages six, seven and eight, following the שכינה from the roof out to the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק matches a key word in the list: roof (גג), wall (חומה), and city (עיר). At this point the שכינה has moved past the walls of the בית המקדש and into the city. The next step proves the stages of the mountain and the wilderness.

keyTerms.meaning: A wall built straight with a plumb line

phrases.english: And from the altar to the roof, as it is written:
"It is better to dwell on a corner of a roof."
phrases.notes: משלי 21:9

phrases.english: From the roof to the wall, as it is written:
"And behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumb line."
phrases.notes: עמוס 7:7

phrases.english: From the wall to the city, as it is written:
"The Lord's voice calls to the city."
phrases.notes: מיכה 6:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of proofs, carrying the שכינה from the מזבח out to the city.
steps.raayaObject: Stages six through eight: מזבח to roof, roof to wall, wall to city.
steps.whyThisMatters: Each פסוק is tied to the list by one key word (roof, wall, city). That pattern helps you follow the whole chain of proofs.

steps.title: Proving the last three journeys of the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the final three stages with פסוקים: from the city to the mountain, from the mountain to the wilderness, and from the wilderness up to its place in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the city to the mountain, as it says: 'God's glory went up from the city and stood on the mountain east of the city.' From the mountain to the wilderness, as it says: 'It is better to dwell in a wilderness land.' From the wilderness it went up to its place, as it says: 'I will go and return to My place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of proofs, giving a פסוק for each of the last three journeys of the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage takes the שכינה one step farther from the people. First it leaves the city for the mountain to its east. Then it goes out to the wilderness, and finally it rises back to Heaven. This completes all ten stages listed back in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The glory of God, meaning His presence
My place, meaning God's place in Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: All ten journeys are now proven from פסוקים. The שכינה left step by step, from the כפורת all the way back up to Heaven.

phrases.english: And from the city to the mountain, as it is written:
"And the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּעֲמֹד עַל הָהָר אֲשֶׁר מִקֶּדֶם לָעִיר״.
phrases.english: and stood upon the mountain which is east of the city."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 11:23

phrases.english: And from the mountain to the wilderness, as it is written:
"It is better to dwell in a wilderness land."
phrases.notes: משלי 21:19

phrases.english: And from the wilderness it went up and settled in its place,
as it is written: "I will go and return to My place, etc."
phrases.notes: הושע 5:15. The word וגו׳ just means "and so on"; the פסוק continues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proofs from step 26 and covers the final three of the ten stages.
steps.raayaObject: The last three stages: city to mountain, mountain to wilderness, wilderness to Heaven.

steps.title: The Divine Presence waited six months for repentance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the שכינה lingered six months in the wilderness, hoping ישראל would do תשובה. When they did not, it gave up on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For six months the שכינה waited for ישראל in the wilderness, in case they would repent. When they did not repent, it said: Let them be lost. As it says: 'The eyes of the wicked will fail, escape is lost from them, and their hope is the breathing out of the soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a detail about the wilderness stage. The שכינה did not leave right away; it waited, hoping for תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the slow, step-by-step departure was a chance for the people to come back. Only after six months with no תשובה did the שכינה give up on them. The פסוק from איוב is the proof: the wicked are left with no escape and no hope.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them be lost (a harsh expression of giving up)
Breathing out of the soul, meaning despair

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the theme behind the whole list of ten journeys. God leaves slowly and keeps the door open for תשובה before fully withdrawing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For six months the Divine Presence lingered
for Israel in the wilderness,
perhaps they would come back in repentance.
Once they did not come back, it said:
Let them be blown away,
phrases.notes: Literally "let their selves be blown out." It's a harsh way of saying "let them be lost."

phrases.english: as it is said: "But the eyes of the wicked shall fail,
and escape is lost from them,
and their hope is the breathing out of the soul."
phrases.notes: איוב 11:20. Notice that מפח sounds like תיפח; that is the link to the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים נִתְעַכְּבָה שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the wilderness stage that was just proven in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה waited six months in the wilderness for ישראל to do תשובה. When they did not, it gave up on them.

steps.title: The סנהדרין's matching exiles begin
steps.stepSummary: Matching the שכינה's ten journeys, the סנהדרין was exiled ten times, known from tradition. The first stages are: from לשכת הגזית to חנות, to ירושלים, and to יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Matching these, the סנהדרין was exiled, and we know this from tradition: from the Chamber of Hewn Stone to חנות, from חנות to ירושלים, and from ירושלים to יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of רבי יוחנן's teaching from step 22. It begins listing the ten places the סנהדרין moved to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the שכינה's journeys, these are not proven from פסוקים; they come from a received tradition (גמרא). The סנהדרין starts in its proper home, לשכת הגזית inside the מקדש. It then moves step by step farther away: to חנות on the Temple Mount, then into ירושלים, then out to יבנה. The list continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: The great court of seventy-one judges
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, the סנהדרין's seat in the מקדש
A place on the Temple Mount outside the main Temple area
A town where the סנהדרין later sat

steps.confusionAlert: Here גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition passed down from teacher to student.

phrases.english: And corresponding to them, the Sanhedrin was exiled, known from tradition:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the ten journeys of the שכינה just listed.

phrases.english: from the Chamber of Hewn Stone to Chanut,
phrases.notes: חנות literally means "shop." Here it is a spot on the Temple Mount, outside the main Temple area.

phrases.english: and from Chanut to Jerusalem,
and from Jerusalem to Yavne,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having finished the שכינה's journeys, the גמרא returns to the second claim of step 22 and begins listing the סנהדרין's ten exiles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין was exiled in ten stages matching the שכינה's, known from tradition. It began with לשכת הגזית, then went to חנות, ירושלים, and יבנה.
